title: feat(plugin-approvals): an empty admin_rescue slate opens on the organization's administrators; retire the unstaffed arm
body:
Fixes #22824

Clause-②: yes

An approval node whose approvers resolve to no concrete person now opens, under the default `onEmptyApprovers: 'admin_rescue'`, on the request organization's administrators, as ordinary approvers in the ordinary inbox. The `unstaffed` queue arm that #22775 added (never published) retires in the same stroke, since the named slate makes it obsolete. Route P1, as ruled (maintainer 「同意 P1」, recorded as `6108375797` on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2057); triage `6108769161`; claim `6108865702`.

## FROM → TO: who receives an `admin_rescue` request

- **FROM:** the request opened on a slate that named no one (the literal `position:NAME`). Measured on this branch's base `efcbac73c`, on a real boot (`bootStack`, the seeded admin owning the default organization): the stored slate was `["position:unstaffed_arm_nobody"]`, the admin's My Pending (`status=pending&approverId=ADMIN_ID,EMAIL`) answered `data: [], total: 0`, their `GET /notifications?type=approval.requested` answered `notifications: [], unreadCount: 0`, and no `sys_inbox_message` row was written. Only the #3424 override could decide it.
- **TO:** the request opens on the holders of the `TENANT_ADMIN` rung of the request's organization: the same authority the tenant arm of `isOverrideActor` trusts (ADR-0095 D3, `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS`), resolved to people. There is no second notion of "admin".

## What changed

**`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`** (`approval-service.ts`)
- `organizationAdministrators(org)`: the candidates are the organization's members (`sys_member.organization_id`, this file's existing answer to "who is in this organization"). Each is asked the rung question over the grants `resolveUserAuthzGrants` (`@objectstack/core`) resolves for them with that organization as the active tenant: the resolver every authorization envelope comes from, so grant windows, deactivated sets, other organizations' scoped grants and position-bound sets answer exactly as when the person acts. No `plugin-security` edit; no better-auth role is read as authority.
- `holdsTenantAdminRung(permissions)` is now the one spelling of the grant read, shared by the tenant arm of `isOverrideActor` (a mechanical swap of the identical expression; its authority does not change) and by the slate.
- Platform administrators are not added for being platform administrators. One who also holds the organization's rung (its owner, say) is on the slate for that rung.
- At node entry, an empty slate under `admin_rescue` (and a `fallback` that found no one either, which already degraded to `admin_rescue`) goes through the SAME `expandApprovers` as `approvers`, as `user` entries in one synthetic group (`#0`). So OOO delegation, the `approverId` index, the `approval.requested` fan-out and `decide` apply unchanged, and a decision by one of them is a slot decision recorded with `via_override: false`.
- The request says why. The abandoned slate and the reason are kept in `__resolvedFrom` as `admin_rescue:abandoned` / `admin_rescue:reason` (the `fallback` branch's flat, policy-prefixed shape), and the timeline carries one system note (`action: 'comment'`, `actor_id: null`, the shape the OOO hop row already uses), for example "Routed to this organization's administrators because the approver slate named no one: position 'sales_manager' has no holder."
- Break-glass stays break-glass. An organization with no administrator, a request with no organization, or an administrator read that fails opens on the slate that names no one, logged as a warning that names which of the three and the fix. A read failure answers a failure, never an invented "nobody".
- The `unstaffed` arm retires: `awaitingRequestIds` and `unstaffedOverridableRequestIds` are removed, and `listRequests` / `countRequests` are byte-identical to their pre-#22775 bodies (compared function by function). `slateNamesAPerson` stays (the open path reads it); its docblock no longer names the arm.

**`@objectstack/spec`**: `IApprovalService.listRequests`' `unstaffed?: boolean` member retires with its docblock. The `limit` docblock keeps #22775's correction minus the arm. The `onEmptyApprovers` `.describe()` text and TSDoc say that `admin_rescue` opens on the organization's administrators and that `fallback` names who decides instead. `content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx` is regenerated (`check:generated --fix`, `check:docs` only).

**`@objectstack/rest`**: `unstaffed` leaves `APPROVAL_REQUEST_LIST_PARAMS` and the multiplicity set, and `readDeclaredQueryBoolean` (its only reader) goes. The file equals the exact reverse-apply of #22775's hunks onto `efcbac73c` (`git apply -R`, then `cmp`). `?unstaffed=` is now refused as an unknown name, `400` with nested `error.code: VALIDATION_ERROR`, before the service runs.

**`@objectstack/lint`**: `approval-approvers-may-resolve-empty` no longer says "waits forever". Both arms say the request opens on the organization's administrators. The hints name `onEmptyApprovers: 'fallback'` as the way to name who decides, and the `os explain` paragraph says the same. Severity, firing conditions and rule ids are unchanged.

**Docs** (`approvals.mdx`): a new "When a slate names no one" section. The manager callout, the `onEmptyApprovers` list, the fallback text, the notification callout and the admin-override callout now describe the administrators' slate. The `unstaffed` filter paragraph and curl are gone.

## The census, first

No shipped consumer of the `unstaffed` member or `?unstaffed` exists outside #22775's own files:
- this repository at `efcbac73c`: every code hit of `unstaffed:`, `?unstaffed`, `.unstaffed` and `'unstaffed'` is in #22775's file list. The only non-test callers of `listRequests` / `countRequests` are the REST handler's two calls;
- objectstack-ai/objectui `origin/main` `1d1cfe0` (read only): `approvalsApi.ts` builds the list query from `status / object / recordId / approverId / submitterId / q / limit / offset` and never sends `unstaffed`. Every other `unstaffed` hit there is the console's own seat label (`approverIdentity.ts`'s `unstaffed: boolean` chip state), not the filter.
- Not published: `npm pack @objectstack/{spec,rest,plugin-approvals}@17.7.0` (npm `latest` is `17.7.0`) holds 0 files matching `unstaffed?: boolean | unstaffedOverridableRequestIds | readDeclaredQueryBoolean`; control: each tarball holds 3–5 files naming `listRequests`.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

1. **Holds.** See FROM above: the real boot at `efcbac73c` stored literals only, listed and counted nothing for the admin, and notified no one.
2. **Partly.** `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS` is declared in `packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`. NO reader resolves "the users holding that rung in organization X": every reader is per user (`resolveUserAuthzGrants`, `derivePosture`, the explain engine). So the slate composes the per-user resolver over the organization's members. Nothing in `plugin-security` was edited.
3. **Partly false.** The `fallback` branch keeps the primary slate's resolution INPUTS (`field:NAME`, `expression#N`) and namespaces its own as `fallback:KEY`. It keeps neither the abandoned slate nor a reason, and a position-only slate writes nothing there (measured: `__resolvedFrom` absent on the boot above). The new keys mirror that flat, prefixed shape (`admin_rescue:abandoned`, `admin_rescue:reason`); there is no second snapshot shape.
4. **Holds.** The member never shipped (the tarball reading above). `check:adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`: exit 0. The new changeset declares no breaking arm, so no disposition marker is owed, and the deleted 22725 row is not a judged status. See Changesets for the one gate that stays red.

## Pins

`src/admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts`: the real `ApprovalService` on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), the real `resolveUserAuthzGrants` over a bound security catalog, and the real `listRequests` / `countRequests` / `getRequest` / `decide` / messaging fan-out:
- a position nobody holds opens on the two administrators (`organization_admin`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`), each one's My Pending lists it with `total: 1` and `viewer.can_act: true`, and each is told once;
- the scene anchored on that slate: a member sees nothing and is told nothing, and a platform admin (unscoped `admin_full_access`) and another organization's administrator are not on it;
- a tenant administrator's decision: `finalized: true`, `approved`, `acted_as` their id, `via_override` false;
- the timeline note and `__resolvedFrom` (exact keys and reason);
- a `fallback` that resolves to no one degrades to the administrators and says so in the reason;
- an administrator out of office is covered by their delegate (`approval.ooo_substituted`), and is not told twice;
- CONTROLS: a staffed slate is unchanged (no administrator, no note); `fallback` opens on its own list; `auto_approve` opens nothing and `fail` refuses (`NO_APPROVERS`); an organization with no administrator gets the slate that names no one, logs it, tells no one, and the platform admin's decision there is an override (`via_override` true).

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-admin-rescue-slate.dogfood.test.ts` (the #22775 dogfood pin, rewritten to the named slate) on a real boot, through the REST door: the seeded admin owns the default organization, and a second member is promoted by a `sys_member` role write, which provisions their capability. Both administrators find the request in My Pending (`total: 1`, `can_act: true`) and hold one `approval.requested` notification. A member sees and holds nothing. The staffed control is unchanged. An administrator's `POST …/approve` is an approval with `via_override` false and the routing note on the timeline. `?unstaffed=true` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

**Retired with the code they pinned**, ⛔ none skipped or disabled: the 9-case `ApprovalService — the unstaffed arm (#22725)` block in `approval-service.test.ts` (the file equals the exact reverse-apply of #22775's hunk), the REST §4 `unstaffed` block (replaced by one refusal pin: `?unstaffed=true|false` answers the full ADR-0112 unknown-name refusal and neither service method runs), and the dogfood arm pin (rewritten above).

## Ablation (one-time, from committed `f3ff683a1`)

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `if (administrators.length) {` with `if (false && administrators.length) {` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `259e3e834b00` → `551f2027d03b`), wrapped in a `trap` restoring `git checkout HEAD --` on an absolute path. The integration file then had **6 failed / 4 passed**: every named-slate case red, and the four controls (staffed, fallback, auto_approve / fail, and the leaderless organization with its override) green. Restore proven: blob `259e3e834b00` equals HEAD's, and `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes. The integration test imports the service from `src`, so no `dist` hop applies. The dogfood pin was not ablated (it reads `plugin-approvals` through `dist`).

## Suites (final runs at `06f9948c8` unless noted)

- `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`: `test` 73 files / 1035 passed; `typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK, the test layer included).
- dogfood, 12 approval-reading files (the new pin, override-composite, my-pending, position-address-readers, flow-node-config, notification-body, activity-text-predicate, both snapshot pins, lookup-title-exposure, seed-ownership-claim-dispatch, audit-log-admin-search): 12 files / 43 passed. `dogfood` `typecheck` exit 0, and its `tsc --listFiles` lists the new pin and fixtures.
- `@objectstack/rest` (at `23a63a18a`; `rest` is unchanged since): `test` 272 files / 5239 passed, 326 skipped; `typecheck` exit 0.
- `@objectstack/lint` (at `23a63a18a`; unchanged since): `test` 137 files / 6416 passed; `typecheck` exit 0.
- `@objectstack/spec` (at `f3ff683a1`; unchanged since): `typecheck` exit 0; `test` 648 files / 19342 passed; `check:generated` all artifacts up to date after the one `gen:docs` regeneration.
- The Dogfood Regression Gate's full population is left to CI.

## Gates (at `06f9948c8`, the final commit)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **116** families (32 paths against merge base `efcbac73c`). Each was run with its exit code recorded to disk before any pipe: **115 exit 0, 1 exit 1**. The one red is `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`, the deliberate correction below. `--ran` reconciliation: "116 derived, 116 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
- Two families first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) on unbuilt packages: `check:skill-examples` (client-react) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. After those packages were built, both exit 0 in the final run. In an earlier run, `check:query-options-erasure` caught two `as any` option erasures this branch had added, and `check-tenant-audit-census` caught the new write call site. Both were fixed (commits `06f9948c8`, `8af84ef80`) and both exit 0 in the final run.
- Lint, narrowed and proven: eslint's population is `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` (`eslint.config.mjs`). `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 24 changed TypeScript files reports 24 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The config sets no `parserOptions.project` (no type-aware linting), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The Markdown and MDX files are outside eslint's population.
- The 49 artifact-roster families, the CI-only jobs and the type-check lanes are left to CI.

## Changesets, and one deliberately red check

- `.changeset/22824-admin-rescue-named-slate.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch (description text), `@objectstack/lint` patch (verdict text). `Clause-②: yes`, stating FROM → TO. `@objectstack/rest` is not listed: against the published 17.7.0, its shipped content does not move.
- **`.changeset/22725-approvals-unstaffed-arm.md` is withdrawn (deleted).** It announces an `unstaffed` arm that this PR retires before it ever ships, so it would publish a false release note. This is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class `check-empty-changeset.mjs` names. `check:empty-changeset --base origin/main` stays **red by design**: Check Changeset is not a required context, and per ruling D the `skip-changeset` label is not applied. **Confirmation requested here:** the 22725 note is withdrawn because the behaviour it describes does not ship.

## File surface beyond the claim's list (declared)

My change turned these red, so each is updated to keep what it pins:
- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` (the rule's `os explain` paragraph) and the rule's hints in `validate-approval-approvers.ts`. The dispatch ruled "the message text only"; the explanation and hints said "waits forever" / "recoverable only by override", which this change makes false, and the os-dev standard clause makes a text this change falsifies a must-fix. The rule's logic is untouched. The conflict is named in the report, not silently resolved.
- `approval-requested-notification.integration.test.ts`: one test name and the header now say "with no organization administrator".
- Dogfood pins whose scene was a slate the administrators' slate now replaces:
  - `approval-override-composite-pin` + fixture route to a named approver who never acts (the override's remaining break-glass case);
  - `my-pending-position-address` and `position-address-readers` + fixtures add a named co-approver, so the `position:NAME` literal stays on the slate for the late holder;
  - `flow-node-config-values-at-registration` asserts the administrators' slate;
  - `activity-text-predicate` and both approval-snapshot pins stamp the holder's organization on the `sys_user_position` rows they seed. The routing read never resolved an unstamped (unknown-tenancy) row, and the literal fallback had masked that.
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`: the routing note's insert is one more write call site (238 → 239, decidable 159 → 160, elevated 126 → 127). Regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, and the census-held prose figures were updated by hand.

## Acceptance notes

- **The abandoned slate is replaced, not kept beside the administrators**, as the ruling's "abandoned primary slate" and the `fallback` branch do. A holder staffed into a position after an all-literal request opened no longer receives it (an administrator can reassign it). A `position:NAME` literal beside a named approver is untouched, and so is the late holder's path to it.
- **Unstamped position assignments.** `expandPositionUsers` matches `sys_user_position.organization_id` by strict equality (the platform's stated fail-closed reading of unknown tenancy, shared with `plugin-sharing`), so an organization-less assignment row never put its holder on a slate. Before, the literal stayed and that holder could still act through the `position:NAME` address. Now an all-literal slate opens on the administrators. Rows written through a door are stamped, and the showcase seed stamps them. Noted, not filed; carrier: none.
- **Cost.** One grant resolution per member of the request's organization, eight at a time, on the empty-slate path only.
- **The submitter is not excluded** from the administrators' slate (a one-admin organization decides its own request), the same as any slate that names its submitter.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json` (the empty-slate fork item) still says `admin_rescue` is "decidable only via the #3424 privileged override". It is internal QA text, not a published surface; carrier: none.
- The `ApproverType` describe text ("a manager step resolves to nobody and the request waits") is still literally true (it waits on the administrators). It was left alone under the describe-only scope.
